title: Khoe languages - Wikipedia
text: The Khoe languages were once considered to be a branch of a Khoisan language family, and were known as Central Khoisan in that scenario. Though Khoisan is now rejected as a family, the name is retained as a term of convenience. The nearest relative of the Khoe family may be the extinct Kwadi language of Angola. title: Khoe–Kwadi languages - Wikipedia
text: The Khoe–Kwadi languages are a family consisting of the Khoe languages of southern Africa and the poorly attested extinct Kwadi language of Angola. The relationship has been worked out by Tom Güldemann, Edward Elderkin, and Anne-Maria Fehn.

title: Khoekhoe language - Wikipedia
text: It belongs to the Khoe language family, and is spoken in Namibia, Botswana, and South Africa primarily by three ethnic groups: Namakhoen, ǂNūkhoen, and Haiǁomkhoen.
